newsitem.title: UK: BOXING-PRINCE NASEEM DESTROYS HARDY IN JUST 93 SECONDS.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-PRINCE NASEEM DESTROYS HARDY IN JUST 93 SECONDS.

text.p: Prince Naseem Hamed fulfilled his pre-bout promises when he defeated challenger Billy Hardy inside the first round of a farcically ill-matched WBO and IBF featherweight title fight on Saturday.

Hamed retained his unified World Boxing Organisation (WBO) and International Boxing Federation (IBF) titles on a technical knock-out after just 93 seconds in which he twice knocked Hardy to the canvas.
In stark contrast, Britain's Robin Reid had to weather a tremendous battle against contender Henry Wharton before retaining his WBC super-middleweight title on a tight points decision.
In the night's other world title fight, Ronald Wright of the United States successfully defended his WBO light-middleweight title by stopping Britain's Steve Foster in the sixth round.
Foster, 32, who had fought 35 professional fights in a career spanning 16 years, announced his retirement immediately after his defeat.
But it was Hamed's fight that topped the bill on a night marketed as "The Best of British".
Hamed, who is not noted for his modesty, had said he would destroy Hardy within the first three minutes. In the end, he needed only half that time.
Hardy, the 32-year-old European champion, was on the canvas after the first real punch of the contest.
He got to his feet but when he buckled again under the impact of a furious left-right-left from Hamed, referee Paul Thomas called the fight to a halt.
Hardy buried his face in his gloves in despair while Hamed, sporting his trademark leopard-skin shorts and, as always, playing to the crowd, celebrated the 26th straight victory of his career.
"I didn't mess about...he was the number one challenger and the prince knocked him out in the first round," Hamed said.
"It takes a bit of something to take someone out in the first round when you make a prediction, and I did it. When I make predictions they come true."
Hardy said: "The first shot he hit me with I honestly felt my nose crack. I'm all numb around my teeth...He's got a kick like a mule, I felt it myself."
In truth though, the fight was a huge disappointment after all the hype which had preceeded it.
Perhaps expecting a totally one-sided contest, many fans had stayed away from the triple-header show and there were plenty of empty seats at Manchester's Nynex arena.

Hamed, who was won 24 of his 26 bouts inside the distance, is now likely to face a much tougher contest against World Boxing Association (WBA) champion Wilfredo Vasquez of Puerto Rico in the United States later this year.
The Reid-Wharton bout was a different story altogether.
Defending champion Reid dominated the early rounds but was often forced to back-peddle later in the contest as a brave Wharton pursued him around the ring.
Wharton was bleeding heavily from the bridge of what looked like a broken nose by the ninth and yet he still managed to summon up the energy to push Reid back against the ropes.
But it was Reid who consistently landed the cleaner punches -- particularly with his left jab -- and in the end, the points decision went his way.
